rows.note: Use this when someone is fussy or hard to please, especially about food or other choices.

example.english: They are very particular; when eating, they always pick the best ones.
example.traditional: 佢好揀擇，食飯一定要揀最靚嗰啲。
example.jyutping: keoi5 hou2 gaan2 zaak6 sik6 faan6 jat1 ding6 jiu3 gaan2 zeoi3 leng3 go2 di1

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose choice for one exact item that has been identified or designated.

example.english: I mean that particular restaurant, not the one next door.
example.traditional: 我講緊指定嗰間餐廳，唔係隔籬嗰間。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gong2 gan2 zi2 ding6 go2 gaan1 caan1 teng1 m4 hai6 gaak3 lei4 go2 gaan1

rows.note: Use this when particular means special or distinguished, as in negative phrases meaning “nothing special.”

example.english: This movie isn't anything particular; once you've watched it, that's it.
example.traditional: 呢套戲冇乜特別，睇完就算。
example.jyutping: ni1 tou3 hei3 mou5 mat1 dak6 bit6 tai2 jyun4 zau6 syun3

rows.note: Use this when a quality or style is characteristic or exclusive to a particular person or thing.

example.english: This flavour is particular to Hong Kong-style diners.
example.traditional: 呢種口味係香港茶餐廳特有嘅。
example.jyutping: ni1 zung2 hau2 mei6 hai6 hoeng1 gong2 caa4 caan1 teng1 dak6 jau5 ge3
